hook: The first author in history|was a *woman*

lines.say: The first author in history whose name we know wasn't Homer. It was a woman named Enheduanna, about forty-three hundred years ago.
shots: line art: Enheduanna disk redraw, slow push

lines.say: She was the daughter of Sargon of Akkad, the first emperor in history. He made her high priestess of the moon god at Ur.
shots: archive: Sargon bronze head (public domain photo)

lines.say: She wrote hymns to the goddess Inanna, and she did something new. She signed them. She wrote in the first person.
In one poem, a rebel has thrown her out of the temple. She writes: he made me walk out. My honey-sweet mouth became foam.
shots: line art: quote text fading in

lines.say: She begs the goddess for help. In the end, she's restored.
Her hymns were copied by student scribes for centuries after she died.
The first writer to say I in literature was a priestess complaining about being kicked out. Writers haven't changed much.

fact_note: Enheduanna, daughter of Sargon of Akkad, en-priestess of Nanna at Ur, c. 23rd c. BC (KNOWN). Hymns incl. Nin-me-sara to Inanna; first-person voice; expulsion by Lugal-Ane and restoration (KNOWN). Quote paraphrases ETCSL translation (KNOWN). Authorship attribution is DEBATED by some scholars. Disk at Penn Museum: check image licence, otherwise redraw. Different angle from TTB's Inanna reel.
ig_caption: the first named author in history was a priestess, and one of her poems is basically her ranting about getting fired
tt_caption: Enheduanna, the world's first known author #history #mesopotamia

hook: A shepherd threw a stone|and found the *oldest Bible*

lines.say: Winter, 1946 to 47. Near the Dead Sea, a young Bedouin shepherd is looking for a lost goat.
He throws a stone into a cave in the cliffs, and hears something break. Pottery.
shots: q: cave opening in cliff Qumran

lines.say: Inside are tall clay jars. Inside the jars, rolled leather scrolls.
Over the next decade, eleven caves give up around nine hundred manuscripts. We call them the Dead Sea Scrolls.
One of them is a complete copy of the book of Isaiah, written over two thousand years ago.
shots: archive: Great Isaiah Scroll (public domain photo)

lines.say: Before that, the oldest full Hebrew copy we had was from around the year 1000. This one was about a thousand years older.
And when scholars compared them, the text was remarkably close. A thousand years of copying by hand, with mostly small differences.
shots: line art: two texts side by side, small differences highlighted

fact_note: Discovery 1946-47, Muhammed edh-Dhib (KNOWN). 11 caves, ~900 manuscripts (KNOWN). Great Isaiah Scroll 1QIsa-a, c. 125 BC (KNOWN). Previous oldest full Hebrew Bible MSS c. 10th-11th c. (Aleppo/Leningrad codices) (KNOWN). Close agreement with Masoretic text, variants mostly minor (KNOWN; extent of variants DEBATED among scholars).
ig_caption: a kid looking for a goat threw a rock into a cave and found manuscripts a thousand years older than anything we had
tt_caption: how the Dead Sea Scrolls were found #deadseascrolls #bible

lines.say: December 1945, Upper Egypt. A farmer named Muhammad Ali al-Samman is digging for soft soil to use as fertilizer near the town of Nag Hammadi.
shots: q: Upper Egypt cliffs Nile fields

lines.say: He hits a sealed jar. He hesitates. It might hold a jinn. Or gold.
shots: q: sealed clay jar in sand

lines.say: He smashes it. Inside: thirteen books bound in leather, written in Coptic.
shots: archive: Nag Hammadi codex leather binding (public domain photo)

lines.say: By his own account, his mother used some of the loose pages to light the oven.
What survived turned out to be early Christian texts that had been lost for over fifteen hundred years. Among them, the Gospel of Thomas.
It has no birth, no crucifixion, no resurrection. Just a hundred and fourteen sayings attributed to Jesus.
shots: line art: list of numbered sayings

lines.say: One of them: split a piece of wood, and I am there. Lift up the stone, and you will find me there.
shots: q: stone turned over in desert

fact_note: Discovery Dec 1945, Muhammad Ali al-Samman, digging for sabakh (KNOWN, his account via James Robinson). Fear of jinn, 13 codices, Coptic (KNOWN). Mother burned pages (KNOWN as his account). Gospel of Thomas, 114 sayings, saying 77 (KNOWN). Thomas date (1st-2nd c.) DEBATED.
ig_caption: some of the lost gospels literally ended up as kindling. 'lift up the stone and you will find me there' lives in my head now
tt_caption: the Nag Hammadi library and the Gospel of Thomas #gospelofthomas #lostgospels

hook: The religion behind|*heaven, hell* and the devil

lines.say: Heaven and hell. A final judgment. A savior at the end of time. The dead rising. Where did these ideas come from?
Many scholars point to Persia, and a prophet called Zarathustra, or Zoroaster. His dates are uncertain, somewhere between three and a half and two and a half thousand years ago.
He taught one supreme good god, Ahura Mazda, at war with a destructive spirit. Every person chooses a side.
shots: line art: light vs dark split

lines.say: After death, souls cross a bridge. For the good it's wide. For the wicked it narrows to a blade.
shots: q: narrow bridge over abyss fog

lines.say: At the end of time, a savior comes, the dead are raised, and evil is destroyed.
In 539 BC, the Persian king Cyrus freed the Jews from Babylon. Some of these ideas show up much more clearly in Jewish texts after that contact.
shots: archive: Cyrus Cylinder replica (public domain photo, non-BM)

lines.say: Borrowed, or developed in parallel? Scholars still argue. But the thread runs through Persia.
shots: line art: thread connecting Persia -> Judea -> Rome

fact_note: Zoroastrian concepts: Ahura Mazda vs Angra Mainyu, Chinvat bridge, Saoshyant, resurrection, final judgment (KNOWN). Zoroaster's dates (DEBATED, c. 1500-500 BC). Cyrus 539 BC (KNOWN). Influence on Second Temple Judaism (DEBATED). Use non-BM Cyrus Cylinder images only.
ig_caption: a lot of what we think of as 'heaven and hell' might trace back to one Persian prophet. the bridge that narrows to a blade is wild
tt_caption: how Zoroastrianism may have shaped heaven and hell #zoroastrianism #religion

lines.say: Around 1350 BC, a pharaoh did something no pharaoh had done. He tried to replace Egypt's gods with one.
His name was Amenhotep the Fourth. He renamed himself Akhenaten, devoted to the Aten, the disc of the sun.
shots: archive: Amarna relief sun disc rays (public domain photo)

lines.say: He built a new capital in the desert, Amarna, and shut down the old temples. Even the art changed: stretched faces, and sun rays ending in little hands.
shots: line art: sun rays ending in hands

lines.say: His hymn to the sun reads strikingly like Psalm 104 in the Bible. Whether one influenced the other is still debated.
shots: line art: two texts side by side

lines.say: When he died, the old priests returned. His son, a boy king we know as Tutankhamun, brought back the old gods.
Akhenaten's statues were smashed, his city abandoned, his name cut from the lists of kings.
They almost succeeded. He was rediscovered only in the 1800s, from the ruins of the city he built.

fact_note: Akhenaten reign c. 1353-1336 BC (KNOWN). Aten worship, Amarna, temple closures, Amarna art (KNOWN). Great Hymn to the Aten vs Psalm 104 similarity (KNOWN; influence DEBATED). Tutankhamun likely his son (DEBATED, DNA suggests so). Damnatio memoriae, omitted from king lists, 'the enemy/that criminal of Akhetaten' (KNOWN). Rediscovered 19th c. (KNOWN).
ig_caption: first one-god experiment in history maybe, and Egypt spent the next decades trying to delete him
tt_caption: Akhenaten, the pharaoh who invented one god #ancientegypt #akhenaten

lines.say: Before dawn, low in the east, there's sometimes a bright light. Brighter than any star. It's Venus, the morning star.
shots: q: Venus morning star before dawn

lines.say: In Latin, the morning star was called Lucifer. Light-bringer.
In the book of Isaiah, the prophet mocks a fallen king of Babylon: how you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn.
In Hebrew it says Helel ben Shachar. When Jerome translated the Bible into Latin around the year 400, he wrote: Lucifer.
Over time, Christian writers read that verse as the fall of Satan from heaven. And the planet's name became the devil's.
shots: archive: Dore fall of Lucifer engraving (public domain)

lines.say: The twist: the same Latin Bible also uses lucifer for the morning star rising in your heart, about Christ.
shots: q: sunrise light heart of clouds
q: Venus close to crescent moon

lines.say: So tomorrow before sunrise, look east. That bright point you see once had the devil's name.
shots: q: eastern horizon dawn silhouette hills

fact_note: Lucifer = Latin morning star (Venus) (KNOWN). Isaiah 14:12, Helel ben Shachar, taunt against king of Babylon (KNOWN). Vulgate rendering 'lucifer' (KNOWN). Later identification with Satan (Origen, Tertullian and others) (KNOWN). 2 Peter 1:19 Vulgate 'lucifer oriatur in cordibus vestris' (KNOWN). Venus visibility as morning star varies by period: TTB should post when Venus is a morning star or adjust last line.
ig_caption: the devil's name started as the name of a planet. you can literally go outside before sunrise and see it
tt_caption: Lucifer originally meant the planet Venus #lucifer #venus

lines.say: Both atheists and believers love to quote Einstein. So what did he actually say about God?
Famous line, from 1926: God does not play dice. But that was about quantum physics, not religion.

In 1929 a rabbi asked him by telegram if he believed in God. He answered: I believe in Spinoza's God, who reveals himself in the harmony of what exists, not in a God who concerns himself with the fates of human beings.
In 1954 he called the word God an expression of human weakness. That letter later sold for nearly three million dollars.
But he also refused to be called an atheist. He said he felt awe at the structure of the universe, and called that feeling religious.
So: no personal God who answers prayers. But not no God at all. Something closer to the order of nature itself.
shots: line art: two crossed-out options, middle highlighted

fact_note: Letter to Max Born, 4 Dec 1926 (KNOWN, 'He does not throw dice'). Telegram reply to Rabbi Herbert Goldstein, April 1929 (KNOWN quote). Gutkind letter 1954, sold at Christie's Dec 2018 for ~$2.9M (KNOWN). Rejected 'atheist' label in several statements (KNOWN). Cosmic religious feeling (1930 essay) (KNOWN).
ig_caption: neither side gets to fully claim Einstein. 'Spinoza's God' is the closest honest answer
tt_caption: what Einstein actually believed about God #einstein #god

lines.say: You've probably seen the meme. Mithras was born of a virgin on December 25th, had twelve disciples, died and rose again. Long before Jesus.
shots: line art: meme-style text list, crossed out one by one later
archive: Mithras tauroctony relief (public domain photo)

lines.say: Mithras was real. A Roman cult god, worshipped in underground temples from about the first century AD.
But here's what the evidence says. Mithras wasn't born of a virgin. Roman art shows him bursting out of a rock, fully grown.
shots: archive: Mithras rock birth relief (public domain photo)

lines.say: No ancient source gives him twelve disciples. And no source says he died and rose again.
shots: line art: three claims, each stamped NO SOURCE

lines.say: December 25th is more complicated. Rome celebrated the Unconquered Sun on that date, and Mithras was sometimes linked with the sun.
Why Christians picked December 25th is genuinely debated. Some historians say to replace the sun festival. Others say it came from calculations about the date of Jesus' conception.
shots: line art: two arrows, two theories

lines.say: So: an interesting mystery cult. But most of the meme isn't in any ancient source.

fact_note: Roman Mithraism 1st-4th c. AD (KNOWN). Rock birth (petra genetrix) (KNOWN). No ancient evidence for virgin birth, 12 disciples, death/resurrection (KNOWN; claims trace to modern authors). Sol Invictus festival 25 Dec, Mithras-Sol association (KNOWN). Origin of Christmas date: history-of-religions vs calculation hypothesis (DEBATED).
ig_caption: I fell for this meme in high school. went back and checked. most of it isn't in any ancient text
tt_caption: Mithras vs Jesus, what the evidence actually says #mithras #christmas

lines.say: Three religious words that started out meaning something completely ordinary.
One. Bible. From the Greek for books, which came from the word for papyrus. And papyrus got its name from Byblos, a port in Lebanon where Greeks bought it.
Two. Satan. In Hebrew, ha-satan means the adversary, or the accuser. In the book of Job, he's not a ruler of hell. He's more like a prosecutor in God's court.
Three. Paradise. From an old Persian word for a walled garden, pairidaeza.
Greek writers used it for the parks of Persian kings. Then Greek translators of the Bible used it for the Garden of Eden.
shots: archive: Garden of Eden painting (public domain)

lines.say: Books, an accuser, a garden. The holiest words were once just everyday ones.

fact_note: Bible < Greek biblia < byblos (papyrus) < Byblos/Gebal (KNOWN etymology). Satan < Hebrew ha-satan 'the adversary/accuser', Job 1-2 heavenly court (KNOWN). Paradise < Old Iranian pairi-daeza via Greek paradeisos (Xenophon), Septuagint for Eden (KNOWN).
ig_caption: paradise literally meant a garden with a wall around it. honestly makes sense
tt_caption: the surprising origins of Bible, Satan and paradise #etymology #religion

hook: Every major religion|fits in the last *17 minutes*

lines.say: Imagine all of human history, three hundred thousand years, squeezed into one day.
Our species appears at midnight. For most of the day, we leave almost no trace of what we believed.
Around four in the afternoon, roughly a hundred thousand years ago, some of the earliest known graves with objects placed beside the dead. Maybe the first hint of an afterlife.
At about five past eleven at night, Göbekli Tepe, the first known temple.
Then everything we call religion today arrives in the last seventeen minutes. The Vedas. Zoroaster. The Hebrew Bible. Buddha. Jesus. Muhammad. Guru Nanak in the last two and a half.
shots: line art: clock 23:43 -> 23:58 with names appearing

lines.say: Which means people were burying their dead with care for tens of thousands of years before any of the religions we know had a name.
The questions are much older than the answers.
shots: line art: clock hand reaching midnight

fact_note: Scale: 300,000 years = 24 h (Homo sapiens, Jebel Irhoud, KNOWN). Earliest burials with grave goods ~100,000-120,000 years (Qafzeh/Skhul; interpretation DEBATED) -> ~16:00. Gobekli Tepe 11,500 yrs -> 23:05. Vedas ~1500 BC (date DEBATED) -> 23:43 = last ~17 min. Guru Nanak c. 1500 AD -> last ~2.5 min. Computed in tools, see commit.
ig_caption: if all of human history was one day, every religion you can name shows up in the last 17 minutes. we were burying our dead with flowers long before that
tt_caption: human history as one day, and when religion appears #history #religion
